title: Prompt Sets, Benchmarks, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood's standards and operational procedures for prompt set creation, benchmark design, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile coordination, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML reviewers, and SREs responsible for model quality and inference economics.

Scope:
- All prompt sets used in the Eval Harness (internal and customer-facing).
- Benchmarks for quality (accuracy/ROUGE/EM), safety, latency-sensitive behavior, and cost-sensitive scenarios.
- Model onboarding steps from evaluation to production rollout.
- Quality guardrails for detecting regressions and performance drift.
- Mapping between quantization profiles and expected metric regressions.
- Regression triage flow and runbook for rapid mitigation and rollback.

Goals:
- Make prompt sets reusable and clearly documented.
- Ensure benchmarks are comparable across model variants and quantization levels.
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist that minimizes surprises in production.
- Reduce mean time to detection (MTTD) and mean time to remediation (MTTR) for regressions.

Ownership and Roles:
- Owner: Applied ML Platform (applied-ml team).
- Stakeholders: Model owners, Runtime engineers, SRE, Security & Compliance.
- Reviewers: see metadata reviewers.

Definitions:
- Prompt Set: A curated collection of prompts and expected outputs for a specific evaluation purpose (e.g., summarization, QA, assistant safety).
- Benchmark: A measurable test suite operating on one or more prompt sets with defined metrics and thresholds.
- Eval Harness: Redwood's test runner that executes prompt sets against model variants, collects metrics, and stores results.
- Quantization Profile: A named configuration describing bit widths, per-layer decisions, and fallback rules applied during model compilation.

Prompt Set Catalog (required fields for every prompt set):
- id: short dash-case identifier (e.g., summarization-news-100).
- owner: team or person (e.g., applied-ml).
- intent: short description of the use-case.
- size: number of examples and a breakdown (train/dev/test if applicable).
- labels: tags (e.g., safety, cost-sensitive, long-context).
- creation_date and last_reviewed date.
- canonical_metrics: list of required metrics (e.g., ROUGE-L, BLEU, F1, pass@k).

Example catalog table (text representation):
| id | intent | size | canonical_metrics | owner | notes |
| summarization-news-100 | News abstractive summarization | 100 examples | ROUGE-L, BLEU | applied-ml | Focus on entity preservation |
| assistant-safety-200 | Safety-critical assistant prompts | 200 examples | toxic_score, hallucination_rate | safety | Include adversarial phrasing |

Designing Benchmarks:
1) Choose prompt sets that reflect production traffic composition (latency, domain, document length distribution).
2) Define fixed metrics and calculation windows. Always include: latency P50/P95, token cost, quality metric (task dependent), and safety metrics where applicable.
3) Use consistent preprocessing (tokenization, normalization). Document any deviations.
4) Run benchmarks across: baseline model, candidate model, and candidate+quantized variants.
5) Store raw outputs and per-example diffs for regression triage.

Standard metrics and alert thresholds (recommended starting points):
- Quality delta: relative drop > 2% absolute or 5% relative on primary metric -> warn; >5% absolute or 15% relative -> critical.
- Latency: P95 increase > 30% over baseline -> warn.
- Token cost: per-token cost increase > 10% without quality improvement -> warn.
- Safety regressions: any increase in toxic_score > 0.5 points or new failure modes -> critical and immediate triage.

Model Onboarding Checklist (must be completed before canary):
1) Eval harness run: baseline and candidate with complete prompt set catalog.
2) Card: Create a Model Onboarding card in the Model Registry with metadata: model_id, weights_hash, quantization_profile, expected_cost_delta.
3) Performance budget: owner defines latency and cost SLOs for target workload.
4) Quality gates: must pass canonical metrics within thresholds above.
5) Safety review: run safety prompt sets and review top-10 failing examples.
6) Quantization impact analysis: run candidate quantized variants and include per-example diff heatmap.
7) Canary plan: rollout percentage schedule, monitoring dashboards, rollback criteria, and on-call escalation list.
8) Stakeholder sign-off: applied-ml lead + runtime owner + SRE.

Quality Guardrails and Monitoring:
- Guardrail tiers:
  - Gate (blocking): fails onboarding if a critical safety or quality gate is violated.
  - Near-term alert: used in canary (e.g., quality delta > threshold).
  - Long-term drift monitor: weekly aggregate checks comparing production to historical baseline.
- Data to capture per request: model_id, model_version, quant_profile, route, latency_ms, token_count, top-3 model outputs, safety_scores, eval_tags.
- Dashboard surfaces: per-route SLOs, per-model quality metrics, per-quantization performance.

Quantization Profiles and Expected Effects:
- Profiles MUST be documented with: name, bit-widths by layer group, expected memory savings, expected throughput improvement, known failure modes, and recommended fallback model variant.
- Recommended experiment matrix: for each profile run 3 seeds and report mean/95CI of quality metrics; compare to full-precision baseline.
- Common mappings: 8-bit symmetric with per-channel scales -> small (<=1%) quality delta for many decoder-only models; 4-bit QAT or advanced recipes -> may introduce bias on rare tokens and require extra evals on safety prompt sets.

Regression Triage Playbook (operational procedure):
1) Detection: Alert received via monitoring or automated eval harness scheduled runs. Identify affected models, quant profiles, and routes.
2) Initial Triage (15-30 mins):
   - Reproduce the regression locally via the Eval Harness on the latest artifacts.
   - Collect top 50 failing examples and diffs versus baseline.
   - Tag examples by failure mode (hallucination, omission, safety, formatting).
3) Severity Assessment (30-60 mins):
   - Map to business impact: customer-facing route? SLA breach? Safety-critical?
   - If safety-critical or high customer impact -> declare incident and page stakeholders.
4) Mitigation Options (select one):
   - Rollback to previous model/quant profile (fastest).
   - Enable fallback routing (route high-risk requests to baseline model).
   - Apply emergency prompt-layer mitigation (prompt templates, output filters).
   - Hotfix model (if feasible and low-risk).
5) Root Cause Analysis (within 72 hours):
   - Compare training / tokenization changes, tokenizers, quantization differences, and runtime kernel changes.
   - Check for correlated infra changes (kernel updates, cuda/runtime).
   - Produce a postmortem with action items and owners.
6) Preventive Actions:
   - Add failing examples to the canonical prompt set(s) and create regression tests.
   - Adjust quantization profile documentation and gating rules if needed.
   - Update onboarding checklist if the failure revealed a coverage gap.

Operational Runbook: Alerts and Playbook Shortcuts:
- Pager escalation matrix: applied-ml oncall -> runtime oncall -> SRE -> ML-denylist owner.
- Quick rollback CLI (example):
  - rwdctl model rollback --model-id <model> --version <previous> --route <route>
- Canary monitoring queries (example PromQL-like filters):
  - avg_over_time(latency_ms{route="assistant"}[10m]) by (model_id)
  - increase_in_quality_metric = (candidate_quality - baseline_quality) / baseline_quality

Examples and Case Studies (brief):
- Case: quantization-induced hallucination (2026-06): 4-bit aggressive profile caused entity hallucination on long-context QA. Mitigation: rollback profile, add prompt set with long-context QA, adopt more conservative per-layer bit allocation.
- Case: tokenizer change mismatch (2025-11): subtle tokenization change introduced repeated tokens in generation. Fix: enforce tokenizer hash check in onboarding card and add auto-check in eval harness.

Appendix / Templates:
- Prompt set template: id, owner, intent, canonical_metrics, created_at, last_reviewed, example_count, example_format, notes.
- Onboarding card checklist (short): eval-harness results, cost estimate, latency SLOs, safety signoff, rollback plan.

References:
- Eval harness standards page: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quality guardrails playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/applied-ml-quality-guardrails-and-regression-triage-playbook-2027
